spec.title: What one more megawatt-hour costs a thermal plant

steps.explanation: Fuel cost per MWh of electricity: the fuel price per MWh of heat divided by the plant's efficiency η. A combined-cycle gas plant (η ≈ 0.55) burns 1.8 MWh of gas per MWh of power.
Carbon cost: emissions per MWh of heat e (gas 0.20, hard coal 0.34, lignite about 0.40 t CO₂) divided by η, times the EU ETS allowance price. The December-2025 EUA averaged about 74 EUR/t in 2025.
Other variable costs: maintenance that scales with running hours, auxiliary materials, start-up wear; a few EUR/MWh.
Gas at 35 EUR/MWh (heat), roughly where the Dutch TTF hub traded for much of 2025.
Imported coal at about 12 EUR per MWh of heat. Carbon is now the larger part of the cost.
Lignite is mined next to the plant and cheap as a fuel, but it is the dirtiest per MWh: its carbon cost alone, about 80 EUR/MWh, is three times a gas plant's 27.
Low efficiency makes peakers the top of the stack: they run only in the scarcest hours.

spec.caption: Illustrative 2025 inputs; fuel prices and efficiencies vary by plant and month. The point: with carbon at around 70–80 EUR/t, gas, hard coal and lignite all land near 90–100 EUR/MWh, which is why the German price so often sits there.
